title: Adversarial review of W0-RECEIPTS (receipts)
final_text:
Review complete. All findings were executed; nothing under `src/` was touched.

**Files written:**
- `review/receipts.md` — the adversarial review
- `probe/render_collision.py`, `probe/render_render_reenter.py` — re-entrancy/deadlock probes
- `probe/activity_runner_errors.py` — runner-error conversion probe
- `probe/bracket_masking.py` — exception-masking probe
- `probe/attacks_failed.py` — four attacks expected to fail (all failed as expected)
- `probe/secret_refusal_fixed.py` — the corrected secret-refusal probe
- `probe/byte_mode_add_only.py` — CRLF/add-only append control

**Findings:**
- **BLOCKER B1** — `bracket()` masks the caller's original exception when the outcome-log call also fails; the probe printed `original exception MASKED by ACTIVITY_LOGGER_FAILED` with no chaining and no record of the real failure.
- **SHOULD-FIX S1** — `activity()` converts only `TimeoutExpired`; a runner raising `OSError` escapes as a bare `OSError`, contradicting "Every way the logger can fail carries a code from the table" (`NON-LoopError OSError` in the probe).
- **SHOULD-FIX S2** — `open_receipt(render=...)` runs user code under the RLock and `flock`; a same-thread re-entry through `ledger_append` deadlocks the process with no exception and no code (SIGALRM-bounded probe exits 3 printing DEADLOCK). The `mint_receipt_id` docstring's "not re-entrant across threads" warning describes the hazard incorrectly (the lock is re-entrant in the *same* thread, which is where render runs).
- **NOTE N1/N2** — process-global `current_receipt()` fallback is racy across threads (no corrupt record constructible, so a note); and the refusal is exactly as strong as the transport's declared credential set.

**Tried and could not break** (all re-run after the last edit): 80 concurrent mints, zero collisions; `SECRET_IN_RECEIPT` refuses with names only, ledger byte-unchanged, for both a registered env and `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY`; cadence miss recorded at notice time with `CADENCE_BACKDATED` refusing a backdate; suffix minting bijective past Z (`...Z AA AB AC AD AE`); CRLF prefix bytes preserved exactly with correct offset accounting.

One honest near-miss is recorded in the review: my first secret probe "succeeded" only because the credential's env name was undeclared — that is the transport's documented declared-set design, and `receipts.py` delegates to it correctly, so it is not a finding.
